text:
jason_support: Customer report — structured output returned invalid JSON when the prompt included a Windows file path with backslashes. Customer gets a parse error when they try to parse the streaming response.

jason_support: Example model output (streaming):
```json
{"files": ["C:\Users\Bob\Documents\Project\n"]}
```

jason_support: Customer error: 'Unexpected end of string at position 42' when feeding the stream into their JSON parser. They also reported billing showing a small charge even though the response was unusable.

lee_engineer: Can you paste the raw streaming chunks from the customer? request_id?

jason_support: request_id: r_2026-03-15-8a7f. Customer provided the exact chunks they received (split across network frames):
```
{"files": ["C:\Users\Bob\Docu
"nts\Project"]}
```

morgan_support: That looks like a classic chunk-boundary break: `\` sequence and the following `"` have been split across two flushes, leaving an unmatched quote in chunk 1. Parser on client sees truncated escape.

anya_prod: :eyes: Was `stream: true` enabled? If so, likely our chunked serializer didn't enforce escape continuity. Short-term workaround for customers: set `structured:false` or switch to `stream:false`. Also customers can pre-escape backslashes in user-provided text (replace `\` with `\\`).

lee_engineer: Captured logs from staging show our JSON-mode streaming writer flushes buffers at 4KB without ensuring trailing backslash sequences are completed. I'll open an internal bug.

jason_support: Sent customer a repro curl they used (streaming example):
```bash
curl -s -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-1","structured":true,"stream":true,"prompt":"list files: C:\\Users\\Bob\\Documents\\Project"}'
```

deploy-bot: Deployed hotfix branch `serializer/escape-guard` to staging (sha abc123) :rocket:

lee_engineer: Hotfix adds lookahead to avoid flushing after a solitary backslash char and adds a small buffer to coalesce escape sequences. Canary rollout to a subset of streaming traffic in ~2h.

jason_support: I'll relay the workaround and ETA to the customer. Offered non-streaming option and suggested server-side pre-escaping as a temporary measure.

anya_prod: Follow-up action: add unit tests for chunked escape sequences and a regression test in the structured-output test harness. Tagging infra and runtime teams for review.

jason_support: Customer confirmed the non-streaming workaround works for their integration. Will mark as resolved after canary completes and monitor for any billing anomalies.
